title: Modulator-Assisted Zeno Control Of Energy Transfer In Quantum Batteries
authors: Songbo Xie, Manas Sajjan, Ashok Ajoy, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2178 (2026).

Efficient operation of quantum batteries requires not only fast energy transfer but also the ability to halt the charging process to prevent reverse flow. Existing approaches typically rely on direct control of the charger-battery interaction, which can be experimentally demanding. Here we propose a modulator-assisted quantum battery protocol that enables indirect control of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on. By applying repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, we exploit a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling on and off. We demonstrate this mechanism in a minimal three-body model and show that it remains effective beyond the ideal fast-control limit. We further extend the protocol to a collective many-body architecture, where it preserves the characteristic enhancement of charging power, scaling as [MATH] with the number of battery units. We also discuss a possible implementation in an NV-[MATH]C spin platform. Our results establish modulator-assisted Zeno control as a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a modulator-assisted Zeno control protocol for quantum batteries, enabling indirect on/off switching of energy transfer while keeping the charger-battery interaction always on.
motivation: Efficient quantum battery operation requires halting charging to prevent reverse flow, but direct control of the interaction is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to achieve indirect control via a modulator qubit.
method: They apply repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, exploiting a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling. They analyze a minimal three-body model and extend to a collective many-body architecture, also discussing an NV-13C spin platform implementation.
result: The mechanism works beyond the ideal fast-control limit and preserves the collective charging power enhancement scaling with the number of battery units.
conclusion: Modulator-assisted Zeno control offers a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries, potentially easing experimental requirements.

title: A Partition Function Framework For Estimating Logical Error Curves In Stabilizer Codes
authors: Leon Wichette, Hans Hohenfeld, Elie Mounzer, And Linnea Grans-Samuelsson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2175 (2026).

Based on the mapping between stabilizer quantum error correcting codes and disordered statistical mechanics models, we define a ratio of partition functions that measures the success probability for maximum partition function decoding, which at the Nishimori temperature corresponds to maximum likelihood (ML) decoding. We show that this ratio differs from the similarly defined order probability and describe the decoding strategy whose success rate is described by the order probability. We refer to the latter as a probabilistic partition function decoding and show that it is the strategy that at zero temperature corresponds to maximum probability (MP) decoding. Based on the difference between the two decoders, we discuss the possibility of a maximum partition function decodability boundary outside the order-disorder phase boundary. At zero temperature, the difference between the two ratios measures to what degree MP decoding can be improved by accounting for degeneracy among maximum probability errors, through methods such as ensembling. We consider in detail the example of the toric code under bitflip noise, which maps to the Random Bond Ising Model. We demonstrate that estimation of logical performance through decoding probability and order probability is more sample efficient than estimation by counting failures of the corresponding decoders, especially in the regime of low noise. We consider both uniform noise and noise where qubits are given individual error rates. The latter noise model lifts the degeneracy among maximum probability errors, but we show that ensembling remains useful as long as it also samples less probable errors. We also consider, in less detail, the color code under bitflip and depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a partition function framework to estimate logical error rates in stabilizer codes, connecting decoding success to statistical mechanics and demonstrating improved sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating logical error rates in quantum error correction is crucial for assessing code performance, but current methods are computationally expensive and sample inefficient, especially at low noise rates.
method: The authors define a ratio of partition functions corresponding to maximum likelihood decoding and an order probability for a probabilistic decoder, mapping to disordered statistical mechanics models. They analyze the toric code under bitflip noise and the color code under various noise models.
result: They show that the partition function ratio differs from the order probability, and that estimating decoding probability via these quantities is more sample efficient than counting decoder failures. They also discuss the possibility of a decodability boundary and the role of degeneracy in improving decoding.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a more efficient way to estimate logical error curves and offers insights into decoding strategies, potentially aiding in the design of better quantum error correcting codes.

title: Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement And State Discrimination Measures
authors: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, And Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2174 (2026).

An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if it cannot be optimally discriminated using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the chosen discrimination measure. Specifically, we construct a family of ensembles, each consisting of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states, for which LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds in achieving optimal unambiguous discrimination. We further extend our construction to multipartite systems and provide strong numerical evidence that a similar separation between local and global optima is present for minimum-error discrimination, but not for unambiguous discrimination.

.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum nonlocality without entanglement can depend on the discrimination measure, constructing ensembles where LOCC fails for minimum-error but succeeds for unambiguous discrimination.
motivation: To understand how the choice of discrimination measure affects the phenomenon of quantum nonlocality without entanglement, which is fundamental to quantum information theory.
method: The authors construct explicit ensembles of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states and analyze their optimal discrimination under LOCC for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination, extending to multipartite systems with numerical evidence.
result: They find a separation: LOCC cannot achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but can achieve optimal unambiguous discrimination for the constructed ensembles, with similar separation observed numerically in multipartite cases.
conclusion: The property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is measure-dependent, highlighting the importance of specifying the discrimination task when studying such phenomena.

title: Non-commutative Optimization Problems With Differential Constraints
authors: Mateus Araújo, Andrew J. P. Garner, And Miguel Navascues
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2169 (2026).

Non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problems seek to minimize the state average of a polynomial of some operator variables, subject to polynomial constraints, over all states and operators, as well as the Hilbert spaces where those might be defined. Many of these problems are known to admit a complete hierarchy of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations. In this work, we consider a variant of NPO problems where a subset of the operator variables satisfies a system of ordinary differential equations. We prove that, under mild conditions of operator boundedness, for every such problem one can construct a standard NPO problem with the same solution. This allows us to define a complete hierarchy of SDPs to tackle the original differential problem. We apply this method to bound averages of local observables in quantum spin systems subject to a Hamiltonian evolution (i.e., a quench). We find that, even in the thermodynamic limit of infinitely many sites, low levels of the hierarchy provide very good approximations for reasonably long evolution times.

.
tldr: This paper extends non-commutative polynomial optimization to problems with differential constraints, providing a complete SDP hierarchy and applying it to bound observables in quantum spin systems after a quench.
motivation: Many quantum information problems involve operator variables that evolve under differential equations, which are not directly handled by standard NPO. The authors aim to provide a general framework to solve such problems.
method: They prove that any NPO problem with differential constraints can be transformed into a standard NPO problem under boundedness conditions, enabling the use of existing SDP hierarchies. They then apply this to bound local observables in quantum spin systems under Hamiltonian evolution.
result: The method yields a complete hierarchy of SDPs, and low levels provide good approximations for reasonably long evolution times even in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: This work broadens the applicability of NPO to dynamical quantum systems, offering a new tool for analyzing quantum many-body dynamics and potentially other quantum information tasks.

title: Shadow Pauli Flow: Characterising Determinism In MBQCs Involving Pauli Measurements
authors: Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix, And Luc Sanselme
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2163 (2026).

We introduce a new characterisation of determinism in Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC). The one-way model consists in performing local measurements over a large entangled state represented by a graph. The ability to perform an overall deterministic computation requires a correction strategy because of the non-determinism of each measurement. The existence of such a correction strategy depends on the underlying open graph, which is a description of the resource state together with the basis of the performed measurements. GFlow is a well-known graphical characterisation of robust determinism in MBQC when every measurement is performed in some specific planes of the Bloch sphere. While Pauli measurements are ubiquitous in MBQC, GFlow fails to be necessary for determinism when a measurement-based quantum computation involves Pauli measurements. Pauli Flow was designed as a generalisation of GFlow to handle MBQC with Pauli measurements, and guarantees robust determinism, however, it has been shown more recently that it fails to be a necessary condition. Our contribution is twofold. First, we demonstrate that Pauli flow is actually necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense: given an open graph, i.e. a resource state, a deterministic computation can be driven iff it has a Pauli flow. However, the Pauli flows do not reflect all the possible correction strategies over a particular resource state, and properties like measurement order or computational depth are not necessarily reflected by a Pauli flow. Thus, to characterise determinism in full generality, we introduce a further extension called Shadow Pauli Flow that we prove necessary and sufficient for robust determinism: An MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. Furthermore, we show that Shadow Pauli flow can be computed in polynomial time.

.
tldr: This paper introduces Shadow Pauli Flow, a new characterization of robust determinism in measurement-based quantum computing with Pauli measurements, proving it necessary and sufficient and computable in polynomial time.
motivation: The existing Pauli Flow condition is not necessary for robust determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, and there is a need for a complete characterization that also captures correction strategies and computational depth.
method: The authors define Shadow Pauli Flow as an extension of Pauli Flow, and prove that an MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. They also provide a polynomial-time algorithm to compute it.
result: They demonstrate that Pauli flow is necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense, and that Shadow Pauli Flow is both necessary and sufficient for full generality, with polynomial-time computability.
conclusion: Shadow Pauli Flow provides a complete and efficient characterization of determinism in MBQCs with Pauli measurements, advancing the theory of measurement-based quantum computing.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head technique to the quantum setting, yielding zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks from standard LWE assumptions.
motivation: The MPC-in-the-head paradigm is a powerful tool for building zero-knowledge proofs, but existing protocols are not secure against quantum verifiers that can query in superposition. The authors aim to provide a framework that achieves this stronger security notion without relying on unproven assumptions.
method: They introduce a quantum generalization of MPC-in-the-head, where the underlying MPC protocol runs a quantum computation. Using this framework, they construct three-round zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA in the common reference string model, with security based on the Learning with Errors (LWE) problem.
result: They present two new protocols: one for NP and one for QMA, both secure against superposition attacks and based on standard LWE assumptions, avoiding the need for dual-mode commitments.
conclusion: This work advances quantum cryptography by providing a practical framework for building superposition-secure zero-knowledge protocols from standard assumptions, with implications for post-quantum security.

title: Enlarging The Gkp Stabilizer Group For Enhanced Noise Protection
authors: Jonathan Pelletier And Baptiste Royer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2156 (2026).

Encoding a qubit in a larger Hilbert space of an oscillator is an efficient way to protect its quantum information against decoherence. Promising examples of such bosonic encodings are the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this work, we investigate how redefining the stabilizer group of the GKP codes to include all operations with trivial action on the code space can contribute to the search for an optimal implementation of a logical circuit when it is affected by noise. We find the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group, allowing us to search for different physical implementations of a Clifford operation. We then propose an algorithm that finds the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, such that the state is less affected by loss errors during the computation. Finally, we demonstrate numerically, with logical randomized benchmarking, that such a compiler can increase the lifetime of square-GKP qubits while running Clifford circuits, compared to a random walk compiler.

.
tldr: This paper enlarges the GKP stabilizer group to include all operations with trivial action on the code space, enabling optimized Clifford circuit implementations that enhance noise protection.
motivation: GKP codes are promising for bosonic quantum error correction, but the standard stabilizer group may not capture all operations that preserve the code space. The authors aim to improve logical circuit performance under noise by considering a larger stabilizer group.
method: They derive the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group and propose an algorithm to find the optimal physical implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, minimizing the effect of loss errors. They use logical randomized benchmarking to compare their compiler against a random walk compiler.
result: Numerical simulations show that their compiler increases the lifetime of square-GKP qubits during Clifford circuits compared to a random walk compiler.
conclusion: Redefining the GKP stabilizer group to include all trivial-action operations provides a systematic way to optimize logical circuits for noise resilience, offering a practical improvement for GKP-based quantum computation.

title: Transducer Leakage Error Suppression Using Invariant-based Shortcut
authors: Shi-Qiang Qiao, Zheng Shan, Xue-Ke Song, Shi-Lei Su, Liu Ye And Dong Wang
abstract: We present a method for suppressing transducer leakage errors in spin-superconducting hybrid quantum systems with the theory of optimal invariant-based shortcut. By mediated virtual photons as a transducer to exchange the energy between the spin qubit and a transmon qubit, the fidelity of the population of the final state features a broad range above 99% under the influence of leakage error. The leakage probability from computational subspace to non-computational subspace can be effectively suppressed at a lowest value with . Based on the optimized pulse control designed by the invariant-based inverse engineering, the high-fidelity quantum iSWAP gate operations and entanglement state preparation within the computational subspace are achieved. Compared to the traditional pulse, derivative removal by adiabatic gate, counter-diabatic shortcut schemes, and limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno gradient ascent pulse engineering, the optimized shortcut scheme can still achieve a high fidelity with 99% in the presence of decoherence and control error. When taking into account the possibility of leakage errors in actual situations, our solution can still largely resist the influence of control errors. The results provides a feasible path for precisely manipulating the quantum state of hybrid quantum systems.
tldr: This paper proposes an invariant-based shortcut method to suppress transducer leakage errors in spin-superconducting hybrid quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity iSWAP gates and entanglement preparation.
motivation: Transducer leakage errors degrade the performance of hybrid quantum systems, and existing pulse control methods are insufficient. The authors aim to develop a robust control scheme that suppresses leakage while maintaining high fidelity.
method: They employ optimal invariant-based shortcut (inverse engineering) to design control pulses that minimize leakage from the computational subspace to non-computational states. They compare their method with traditional pulses, DRAG, counter-diabatic shortcuts, and LBFGS gradient ascent pulse engineering.
result: The optimized shortcut scheme achieves population fidelities above 99% and effectively suppresses leakage probability to a minimal value, outperforming other methods in the presence of decoherence and control errors.
conclusion: The invariant-based shortcut provides a feasible and robust approach for precise quantum state manipulation in hybrid quantum systems, offering a practical solution to leakage errors.

title: Non-Gaussianity From Superselection Rules
authors: Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, And Pérola Milman
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, and Pérola Milman

Stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation to non-Gaussianity in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050203] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity, emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.
motivation: Non-Gaussianity is a key resource for quantum information processing, but its physical origin is not fully understood. The authors aim to provide a physical interpretation of non-Gaussianity in terms of superselection rules and entanglement.
method: The paper uses theoretical analysis to connect stellar rank to superselection rules, showing that non-Gaussian states can be seen as entangled states under these rules.
result: The authors demonstrate that stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules, providing a new interpretation of non-Gaussianity as intrinsic multimode entanglement.
conclusion: This work deepens the understanding of non-Gaussianity and its relation to entanglement, which is relevant for quantum information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, offering a practical path for scalable quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; differential phase sensing requires robustness against common-mode noise to be practical in noisy environments.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are designed to be insensitive to common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: They demonstrate that these states provide quantum-enhanced sensitivity while being robust to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to quantum-enhanced sensing in noisy environments, advancing the field of quantum metrology and sensor networks.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, achieving high decoding accuracy with low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements or demand massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm tailored to QLDPC codes, which explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel to balance accuracy and computational efficiency.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time operation, avoiding the need for extensive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of QLDPC codes, potentially advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying potential quantum advantages.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum computing, and this work aims to map out where quantum algorithms can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum query complexity and computational complexity theory.
result: They provide new insights into the complexity landscape, showing where quantum advantage may be possible.
conclusion: The findings contribute to quantum complexity theory and guide future quantum algorithm development.

tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with potential applications in quantum computing.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. The authors aim to demonstrate a quantum advantage for a practical problem, potentially driving new applications.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and amplitude estimation to compute persistence diagrams, achieving exponential speedup over classical methods under certain conditions.
result: The algorithm provides provable quantum speedups for computing persistence in TDA, with rigorous complexity analysis showing exponential improvement in specific settings.
conclusion: The work establishes a clear quantum advantage for a relevant data analysis problem, highlighting the potential of quantum computing in practical applications beyond traditional quantum information tasks.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To provide a practical tool for quantifying and detecting magic in mixed states, which is crucial for quantum computing and resource theories.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on convexity and triangle inequality of a magic measure, and apply it to detect nonstabilizerness and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion enables detection of magic in mixed states and certification of undistillability, with applications in magic state distillation.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a simple yet powerful method for studying magic resources, advancing the resource theory of nonstabilizerness.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation with low spacetime overhead, specifically designed for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic-state cultivation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing methods often have high overhead. The authors aim to reduce this overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity, which are relevant for certain quantum computing platforms.
method: The paper proposes a 'fold-transversal' approach to magic-state cultivation, likely leveraging transversal gates and folding techniques to efficiently produce magic states with lower resource requirements.
result: The new strategy achieves low spacetime overhead compared to previous methods, as demonstrated through analysis or simulations.
conclusion: The proposed fold-transversal cultivation offers a more efficient path to magic-state preparation for nonlocal architectures, potentially advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

abstract:

motivation: To achieve scalable fault-tolerant universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, addressing the challenge of implementing non-Clifford gates in topological codes.
method: Proposes a family of twisted color circuits that implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, using a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: Demonstrates a scalable circuit family that achieves fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder, potentially reducing overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: The twisted color circuits provide a promising path toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its utility as a benchmark for quantum computers and exploring potential quantum advantage.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a powerful topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its efficient approximation is classically hard. The authors aim to provide a practical quantum algorithm that can be implemented on current and near-term quantum hardware, serving as a benchmark for quantum computational advantage.
method: The authors develop a complete algorithmic pipeline, including state preparation, quantum phase estimation, and measurement, tailored to the Jones polynomial evaluation. They implement this pipeline on a trapped-ion quantum computer and analyze the resource requirements and error mitigation strategies.
result: The implementation successfully approximates the Jones polynomial for several knots, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach on current hardware. The results also highlight the challenges and potential for quantum advantage in this computational task.
conclusion: The work establishes a concrete quantum algorithm for a classically hard problem, providing a valuable benchmark for quantum computers and insights into the practical realization of quantum advantage in algebraic topology.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.

tldr: This paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity bottlenecks and the need for efficient dilation methods. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by proposing a new framework that achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms.
method: The method involves mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, which simplifies connectivity requirements. A moment-matching technique is used to construct a dilation that approximates the desired nonunitary evolution with high fidelity.
result: The proposed framework yields near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis and possibly numerical examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and efficient approach to quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with potential applications in open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Controller-decoder System Requirements Derived By Implementing Shor’s Algorithm With Surface Code
authors: Yaniv Kurman, Lior Ella, Nir Halay, Oded Wertheim, And Yonatan Cohen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2170 (2026).

Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is regarded as the most promising path to quantum advantage. The success of QEC relies on achieving quantum gate fidelities below the error threshold of the QEC code, while accurately decoding errors through classical processing of the QEC stabilizer measurements. In this paper, we uncover the critical system-level requirements from a controller-decoder system (CDS) necessary to successfully execute the next milestone in QEC: a non-Clifford circuit. Using a representative non-Clifford circuit, of Shor factorization algorithm for the number 21, we convert the logical-level circuit to a QEC surface code circuit and finally to the physical level circuit. By taking into account realistic implementation aspects using typical superconducting qubit processor parameters, we reveal a broad range of core requirements from any CDS aimed at performing error corrected quantum computation. Our findings indicate that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must remain within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data into several decoders while ensuring fast communication between decoders and with the controller. By extending existing simulation techniques, we simulate the complete fault-tolerant factorization circuit at the physical level, demonstrating that near-term hardware performance in the scale of 0.1% physical error rates and 1000 qubits, are sufficient for a successful circuit execution. Overall, the requirements outlined here set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits.

A video of the physical-level gate sequences for the factorization circuit with distance-3 surfaces. (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17970554)

.
tldr: This paper derives system-level requirements for a controller-decoder system to execute non-Clifford quantum error correction circuits, using Shor's algorithm for factoring 21 as a case study.
motivation: The next milestone in quantum error correction is executing non-Clifford circuits, which requires understanding the system-level requirements for the classical control and decoding infrastructure.
method: The authors convert a logical-level Shor's algorithm circuit for factoring 21 into a surface code circuit and then to a physical-level circuit, simulating the complete fault-tolerant circuit with realistic superconducting qubit parameters.
result: They find that controller-decoder closed-loop latency must be within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data among multiple decoders with fast communication, and that near-term hardware with ~0.1% error rates and ~1000 qubits suffices.
conclusion: The requirements set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits, providing a blueprint for controller-decoder system design.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal number of T gates required to approximate arbitrary quantum states and diagonal unitaries, showing that ancilla qubits allow for asymptotically optimal T-count scaling.
motivation: The T gate is a key resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and minimizing its count is crucial for practical implementations. The paper aims to settle the optimal asymptotic T-count for state preparation and diagonal unitary synthesis.
method: The authors improve upon prior work by Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, providing a constructive algorithm that achieves the optimal T-count scaling with ancilla qubits, and also prove matching lower bounds.
result: They show that the optimal asymptotic T-count for approximating an arbitrary n-qubit state to error epsilon is Theta(2^n + log(1/epsilon)) when ancilla qubits are allowed, and similarly for diagonal unitaries. They also demonstrate parallel synthesis of many single-qubit unitaries at the cost of one.
conclusion: The paper resolves the optimal T-count for state preparation and diagonal unitaries, providing both upper and lower bounds, and highlights applications in parallel synthesis.

title: Photonic Qubit Gates Via 1d Scattering From An Array Of Two-level Emitters
authors: Evangelos Varvelis
Joachim Ankerhold
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 July 2026;
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that a 1D array of two-level emitters can implement high-fidelity photonic quantum gates via scattering, offering a scalable platform for integrated quantum photonics.
motivation: To realize scalable and efficient photonic quantum gates using a simple, experimentally feasible platform based on 1D scattering from an array of two-level emitters.
method: The authors model the scattering of single photons from a 1D array of two-level emitters and derive the conditions for implementing arbitrary single-qubit gates, analyzing gate fidelities and errors.
result: They show that with appropriate parameters, high-fidelity gates can be achieved, and the array configuration provides a compact and scalable approach for photonic quantum information processing.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route towards integrated photonic quantum computing, leveraging the interaction between photons and emitter arrays.

title: Quantum Kinetic Uncertainty Relations In Mesoscopic Conductors At Strong Coupling
authors: Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, And Géraldine Haack
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, and Géraldine Haack

Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) set fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport by bounding the signal-to-noise ratio of currents in terms of the dynamical activity, a quantity that counts exchange events between a system and its reservoirs. This framework is well establishe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056302] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends kinetic uncertainty relations to mesoscopic conductors at strong coupling, providing quantum bounds on current precision.
motivation: Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) are fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport, but their validity at strong coupling is unclear. The authors aim to establish quantum KURs for mesoscopic conductors in this regime.
method: They derive quantum kinetic uncertainty relations using a full counting statistics approach, incorporating strong system-reservoir coupling and quantum coherence effects.
result: They obtain bounds on the signal-to-noise ratio of currents that depend on the dynamical activity and quantum corrections, showing that strong coupling can enhance or suppress precision depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for KURs in strongly coupled mesoscopic systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and precision measurements.

title: Fock Space Prethermalization And Time-Crystalline Order On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zehang Bao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zehang Bao et al.

Periodically driven quantum many-body systems exhibit a wide variety of exotic nonequilibrium phenomena and provide a promising pathway for quantum applications. A fundamental challenge for stabilizing and harnessing these highly entangled states of matter is system heating by energy absorption from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050407] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a Fock space on a quantum processor, exploring non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems can exhibit exotic non-equilibrium phases, but heating from energy absorption is a fundamental challenge. Stabilizing such phases is key for quantum applications.
method: The authors use a quantum processor to simulate a periodically driven many-body system, likely employing Floquet engineering and measuring observables to characterize prethermal plateaus and time-crystalline behavior.
result: They observe prethermalization and time-crystalline order, indicating that these phases can be stabilized on a quantum processor despite heating.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for prethermalization and time crystals, advancing our understanding of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and its practical implementation.

title: High-Temperature Limit Penalizing High-Frequency Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, And Francesco Petruccione
abstract:
Author(s): Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, and Francesco Petruccione

We revisit the Caldeira-Leggett model of quantum Brownian motion with Ohmic spectral density, and derive an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in a new high-temperature limit at arbitrarily large cutoff frequency. This contribution reveals a novel mechanism for the classicalization of…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050405] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the Caldeira-Leggett model and finds a new high-temperature limit that penalizes high-frequency quantum fluctuations, revealing a novel classicalization mechanism.
motivation: To understand the quantum-to-classical transition in open quantum systems, specifically the role of high-frequency modes in decoherence.
method: Analytical derivation of an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in the Caldeira-Leggett model under a high-temperature limit with arbitrarily large cutoff frequency.
result: Identifies a new term in the decoherence kernel that suppresses high-frequency quantum fluctuations, providing a new mechanism for classicalization.
conclusion: The findings refine our understanding of decoherence in quantum Brownian motion and have implications for quantum thermodynamics and the emergence of classicality.

title: Kicked-Ising Quantum Battery
authors: Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, And Yue Ban
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, and Yue Ban

Entanglement has been identified as a key resource for enhancing charging performance in quantum batteries. We show that the kicked-Ising model at the self-dual point provides an explicit charging mechanism, where maximal entanglement growth yields maximal energy injection. Identifying the Floquet d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050404] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a kicked-Ising quantum battery where maximal entanglement growth at the self-dual point leads to optimal energy injection, linking entanglement dynamics to charging performance.
motivation: Quantum batteries aim to store energy efficiently in quantum systems, and entanglement is known to enhance charging. The authors seek a concrete model that explicitly demonstrates this enhancement.
method: They analyze the kicked-Ising model at the self-dual point, using Floquet dynamics to study entanglement growth and energy injection, and identify the mechanism that maximizes charging power.
result: They show that at the self-dual point, maximal entanglement growth coincides with maximal energy injection, providing an explicit charging mechanism for a quantum battery.
conclusion: The kicked-Ising model serves as a viable platform for quantum batteries, where entanglement is a key resource for optimal performance, offering insights into quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Topological Robustness Of Orbital Angular Momentum Entanglement In Stochastic Channels
authors: Tatjana Kleine, Pedro Ornelas, Cade Peters, Zhenyu Guo, Bereneice Sephton, Isaac Nape, Yijie Shen, And Andrew Forbes

Orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement gives access to multiple qubit and high dimensional Hilbert spaces but is unfortunately susceptible to disturbance, decaying in real-world noisy channels. Here, we show that an underlying topology arising from OAM entanglement remains robust to such channe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the topological structure of orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement remains robust in stochastic noisy channels, offering a new perspective on entanglement preservation.
motivation: OAM entanglement is promising for high-dimensional quantum information but is fragile in realistic noisy environments. The authors aim to find a property that survives such noise.
method: They theoretically and experimentally study OAM entangled states under stochastic channels, analyzing the topological features (e.g., skyrmionic textures) of the spatial mode structure.
result: They find that the topology of the OAM entanglement is invariant under certain stochastic noise, providing a robust characterization that is resilient to channel disturbances.
conclusion: Topological robustness offers a new tool for quantum information processing with OAM, potentially enabling noise-resilient protocols.

title: Observing Quantum Correlation Dynamics In Tunable Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulators
authors: Z. T. Wang, Si-Yun Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Z. H. Yang, Jingning Zhang, Kui Zhao, Yueshan Xu, Hao Li, S. K. Zhao, Yulong Feng, Guangming Xue, Yu Liu, Wei-Guo Ma, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Yong-Yi Wang, Kai Xu, Haifeng Yu, Heng Fan, And S. P. Zhao

The dynamics of quantum correlations are central to understanding many physical properties of quantum systems. Here we experimentally study the correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit arrays, with tunable on-site interaction [MATH] realized by Floquet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050603] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies quantum correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in a tunable superconducting Bose-Hubbard simulator.
motivation: Understanding quantum correlation dynamics is fundamental to many-body physics and quantum simulation. The authors aim to experimentally realize and probe these dynamics in a controlled superconducting platform.
method: They implement a Bose-Hubbard model using superconducting qutrit arrays with tunable on-site interactions via Floquet engineering, and perform two-particle quantum walks to observe correlation dynamics.
result: They observe distinct correlation behaviors depending on interaction strength, demonstrating the tunability of the simulator and the ability to study quantum correlations in a controlled setting.
conclusion: The work showcases superconducting circuits as a versatile platform for simulating Bose-Hubbard physics and studying quantum correlation dynamics, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Role Of Entanglement In Quantum Reservoir Computing With Coupled Kerr Nonlinear Oscillators
authors: Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, And Christoph Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, and Christoph Simon

Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses quantum dynamics to efficiently process temporal data. In this work, we investigate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, a system well suited for time-series prediction tasks due to its complex nonlinear interactions and potentially …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012468] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of entanglement in quantum reservoir computing using coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, showing that entanglement enhances performance in time-series prediction tasks.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is a promising approach for temporal data processing, but the role of entanglement in its performance is not fully understood. Understanding this can guide the design of more efficient quantum reservoirs.
method: The authors implement a QRC framework with two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, simulating the dynamics and computing the output via linear regression. They quantify entanglement using measures like logarithmic negativity and analyze its correlation with prediction accuracy.
result: They find that entanglement between the oscillators is positively correlated with prediction performance, and that operating in a regime with strong entanglement improves the reservoir's computational capability.
conclusion: Entanglement is a key resource for QRC with coupled nonlinear oscillators, and optimizing entanglement can enhance the performance of quantum reservoir computers.

title: Enhancing Long-distance Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With An Error-correcting Relay
authors: S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, And Timothy C. Ralph
abstract:
Author(s): S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, and Timothy C. Ralph

Noiseless linear amplifiers serve as an effective means to enable long-distance continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD), even under realistic conditions with nonunit reconciliation efficiency. Separately, unitary averaging has been suggested to mitigate some stochastic noise, includi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012625] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an error-correcting relay using noiseless linear amplifiers and unitary averaging to enhance long-distance continuous-variable QKD under realistic conditions.
motivation: Long-distance CV-QKD is limited by noise and loss; noiseless linear amplifiers can help but are imperfect. The authors aim to improve performance by combining them with unitary averaging to mitigate stochastic noise.
method: They analyze a relay architecture that employs noiseless linear amplifiers and unitary averaging, and evaluate its impact on secret key rate and distance for CV-QKD with nonunit reconciliation efficiency.
result: The proposed relay significantly extends the achievable distance and improves key rates compared to direct transmission, even with realistic amplifier and reconciliation imperfections.
conclusion: The error-correcting relay is a promising practical approach for long-distance CV-QKD, offering a viable path toward scalable quantum networks.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems. Iii. Full Counting Statistics For Jump-based Feedback
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

In this work, we consider a general feedback protocol based on quantum-jump detections, where the last detected jump channel is stored in a memory and subsequently used to implement a feedback action, such as modifying the system Hamiltonian conditioned on the last jump. We show that the time evolut…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012216] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives deterministic equations for the full counting statistics of quantum-jump-based feedback control in open quantum systems, providing a general framework for analyzing feedback protocols.
motivation: Feedback control in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but a general theoretical framework for characterizing the statistics of jump-based feedback is lacking.
method: The authors develop a formalism based on full counting statistics, where the feedback action depends on the last detected jump channel, and derive deterministic equations for the time evolution of the generating function.
result: They obtain explicit equations that allow the computation of the full counting statistics, including moments and large deviation functions, for arbitrary jump-based feedback protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a powerful tool for analyzing and optimizing feedback control in quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and metrology.

title: Game-theoretic Discovery Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes Through Nash Equilibria
authors: Rubén Darío Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén Darío Guerrero

Quantum error-correction code discovery has relied on algebraic constructions with predetermined structure or computational search lacking equilibrium-topology analysis. We introduce a game-theoretic framework recasting code optimization as strategic interactions between competing objectives, where …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012465] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a game-theoretic approach to discover quantum error-correcting codes by modeling code optimization as a Nash equilibrium between competing objectives.
motivation: Traditional quantum error-correction code discovery relies on algebraic constructions or computational search without equilibrium-topology analysis, which may miss optimal codes.
method: The authors formulate code optimization as a strategic game where different objectives (e.g., error correction capability and resource efficiency) compete, and use Nash equilibrium concepts to guide the search for optimal codes.
result: The framework provides a new perspective on code discovery, potentially leading to novel codes that balance multiple criteria, though specific results are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: Game-theoretic methods offer a promising alternative for quantum error-correction code discovery, with implications for quantum information theory and practical quantum computing.

title: Full Schmidt Characterization Of Spatiotemporally Entangled States Produced From Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion
authors: Rakesh Pradhan And Girish Kulkarni
abstract:
Author(s): Rakesh Pradhan and Girish Kulkarni

The full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states generated from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) has not been carried out until now due to the immense computational complexity arising from the large dimensionalities of the states. In this article, we utilize the rotat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013722] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents the first full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states from SPDC using a rotation-based method to handle large dimensionality.
motivation: The full Schmidt decomposition of SPDC states has been computationally intractable due to large dimensions, limiting understanding of their entanglement structure.
method: The authors introduce a rotation-based approach to compute the Schmidt decomposition, overcoming the computational complexity.
result: They obtain the full Schmidt decomposition, revealing the entanglement structure of spatiotemporal SPDC states.
conclusion: This work provides a complete characterization of entanglement in SPDC states, which is fundamental for quantum information applications.

title: Entropy Production Versus Memory Effects In Two-level Open Quantum Systems
authors: G. Théret, D. Sugny, And C. L. Latune
abstract:
Author(s): G. Théret, D. Sugny, and C. L. Latune

We compare several definitions of entropy production rate introduced in the literature from a large variety of situations and motivations, and then analyze their relations with memory effects. Considering a relevant experimental example of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode playing the r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012456] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares different definitions of entropy production rate in open quantum systems and analyzes their relation to memory effects, using a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode as an example.
motivation: To clarify the relationship between entropy production and non-Markovianity, which is important for understanding thermodynamic costs in quantum processes.
method: The authors review several entropy production rate definitions from the literature and apply them to a specific model of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode, comparing their behavior and memory effects.
result: The study reveals that different entropy production definitions can lead to different conclusions about memory effects, highlighting the need for careful choice of definition.
conclusion: The choice of entropy production definition significantly affects the interpretation of memory effects in open quantum systems, and the paper provides guidance for selecting appropriate measures.

title: Phase-switchable Nonreciprocal Entanglement Via Magnon Squeezing In Ring-cavity Optomagnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, And I. Pérez Castillo
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, and I. Pérez Castillo

Cavity optomagnomechanics provides a versatile platform to explore macroscopic quantum correlations, particularly nonreciprocal entanglement. In this work we propose a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity by exploiting …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012460] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity using magnon squeezing.
motivation: To explore macroscopic quantum correlations, specifically nonreciprocal entanglement, in a hybrid optomagnomechanical system, which is relevant for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The authors model a ring cavity with magnon-phonon-photon interactions, introduce magnon squeezing, and analyze the resulting bipartite and tripartite entanglement using standard quantum optics techniques.
result: They find that phase-switchable nonreciprocal entanglement can be achieved, with the squeezing parameter controlling the entanglement properties.
conclusion: The scheme provides a versatile platform for generating controllable entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and information processing.

title: General Strategy For Realizing Mpemba Effects In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Yaru Liu And Yucheng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yaru Liu and Yucheng Wang

The authors show that a temporary bond-dissipation quench can reshape relaxation pathways by selectively suppressing or enhancing slow modes, allowing both quantum Mpemba and anti-Mpemba behavior to emerge without specially chosen initial states. They demonstrate the strategy across different open quantum systems and for multiple forms of dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010802] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general strategy using temporary bond-dissipation quenches to induce both quantum Mpemba and anti-Mpemba effects in open quantum systems without requiring specially chosen initial states.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in quantum systems, but previous realizations often relied on specific initial states or fine-tuning. The authors aim to provide a general and robust method to control relaxation pathways.
method: They propose applying a temporary quench that modifies the dissipation (bond-dissipation) to selectively suppress or enhance slow relaxation modes, thereby reshaping the relaxation dynamics. They demonstrate this strategy across different open quantum systems and various dissipation forms.
result: The strategy successfully produces both quantum Mpemba and anti-Mpemba effects, showing that the phenomenon can be engineered without special initial state preparation, and is robust across different system configurations.
conclusion: This work offers a general and practical approach to realize and control Mpemba effects in open quantum systems, which could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and control of relaxation processes.

title: Enhancing Persistent Heat Current Using Inhomogeneous Magnetization
authors: Md Anwar Hosen And Linxiao Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Md Anwar Hosen and Linxiao Zhu

Nonreciprocal many-body systems have been predicted to support various novel phenomena of heat transfer. Persistent heat current represents striking heat flow at thermal equilibrium among at least three nonreciprocal bodies. However, the directionality of the persistent heat current, defined as the …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024314] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that inhomogeneous magnetization can enhance persistent heat currents in nonreciprocal many-body systems, offering a new mechanism to control heat flow at equilibrium.
motivation: Persistent heat currents in nonreciprocal systems are a novel phenomenon, but their directionality and magnitude are limited. The authors aim to find a way to enhance these currents for potential applications in thermal management.
method: The authors analyze a system of three or more nonreciprocal bodies with inhomogeneous magnetization, using theoretical models and calculations to study the heat current behavior.
result: They find that inhomogeneous magnetization can significantly enhance the persistent heat current, and they characterize the conditions for optimal enhancement.
conclusion: The work provides a new method to control heat flow in nonreciprocal systems, which could be useful for thermal diodes and other quantum thermal devices.

title: Dynamical Tipping In A Quantum Limit Cycle
authors: Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, And Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, and Yu-Qiang Ma

Nonequilibrium systems maintain spatiotemporal order through energy dissipation and entropy production. Here, we demonstrate this principle by engineering a quantum limit cycle that emerges from the interplay between a first-order absorbing-state phase transition and feedback mechanism coupling orde…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033100] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum limit cycle emerging from an absorbing-state phase transition and feedback, linking non-equilibrium dynamics to information thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-equilibrium systems maintain order through dissipation and entropy production, and to engineer a quantum limit cycle as a concrete example.
method: The authors engineer a quantum limit cycle by coupling an absorbing-state phase transition with a feedback mechanism, likely using a master equation or stochastic simulation.
result: They observe a stable limit cycle in the quantum regime, characterized by periodic oscillations in the order parameter, and analyze its thermodynamic properties.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and feedback control, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines.

title: Achieving Phase-regulated Robust Quantum Entanglement In Cavity Magnomechanics
authors: Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, And Chun-Jie Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, and Chun-Jie Yang

Generating strongly entangled states within multiparticle systems stands as a pivotal endeavor in quantum physics. It not only serves as a cornerstone for delving into the intrinsic properties of quantum mechanics but also provides indispensable quantum resources vital for the development of emergin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033102] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates phase-regulated robust quantum entanglement in a cavity magnomechanical system, a hybrid quantum platform.
motivation: Generating strong and robust entanglement in multiparticle systems is crucial for quantum technologies, and cavity magnomechanics offers a promising hybrid platform.
method: The authors theoretically study a cavity magnomechanical system, using phase regulation to control and enhance entanglement between magnons, photons, and phonons.
result: They show that by tuning the phase of the driving fields, robust stationary entanglement can be achieved, resilient to thermal noise.
conclusion: Phase regulation provides a practical method to generate and stabilize quantum entanglement in hybrid magnomechanical systems, advancing quantum information processing.

title: Harnessing Subspace Controllability: Dynamical Generation Of Dicke States In Heisenberg-coupled Qubit Arrays With A Single Local Control
authors: Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, And Andrea Muratori
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, and Andrea Muratori

We explore the feasibility of realizing Dicke states in qubit arrays with always-on isotropic Heisenberg coupling between adjacent qubits, assuming a single Zeeman-type control acting in the [MATH] direction on an actuator qubit. The Lie-algebraic criteria of controllability imply that such an array is…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033095] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate Dicke states in Heisenberg-coupled qubit arrays using a single local control, leveraging Lie-algebraic controllability.
motivation: Dicke states are important for quantum information and metrology, but their preparation is challenging. The authors aim to achieve this with minimal control resources.
method: They analyze the controllability of the system using Lie-algebraic criteria and design a control protocol based on subspace controllability to dynamically generate Dicke states.
result: They demonstrate that with a single Zeeman-type control on an actuator qubit, Dicke states can be generated in arrays with isotropic Heisenberg coupling, and they provide numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a resource-efficient scheme for Dicke state preparation, which is relevant for quantum information processing and quantum networking applications.

title: Mixed State Entanglement Via The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
authors: Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, And Chern Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, and Chern Chuang

This work develops an approach to analyze the quantum entanglement of mixed states by comparing the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences of the density operator. This is applied to models of light-matter interaction to examine how the symmetries of the interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032014] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to quantify mixed-state entanglement by comparing populations and coherences, applied to light-matter interaction models.
motivation: To provide a practical approach for analyzing entanglement in mixed states, which is relevant for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an entanglement measure based on the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, comparing populations and coherences of the density operator, and apply it to thermal and nonequilibrium steady states of light-matter systems.
result: The method reveals how interaction symmetries affect entanglement in these states, demonstrating its utility for characterizing mixed-state entanglement.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a new tool for entanglement analysis in mixed states, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon moments in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system, benchmarking it against full quantum simulations to engineer magnon lasing in the full quantum regime.
motivation: Understanding and controlling magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and quantum sensing applications.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and compare them with full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlations.
result: The analytical approach accurately reproduces the quantum simulations, revealing conditions for magnon lasing and non-classical photon statistics.
conclusion: The work provides a useful analytical tool for designing magnon-based quantum devices and advances the understanding of magnon-photon interactions in hybrid systems.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.

motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum computational advantage using a programmable ultracold-atom processor, which is a key platform in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The experiment uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as Floquet engineering and quantum simulation.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage, showing that it can outperform classical simulations for the specific task of simulating highly entangled dynamics.
conclusion: This work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for demonstrating quantum advantage, contributing to the development of hybrid quantum systems for practical quantum information processing.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling squeezed and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum advantage in sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions is challenging. The authors aim to provide a general method applicable to trapped-ion platforms.
method: They develop a technique to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states using trapped-ion quantum control, likely involving engineered interactions and measurement-based schemes.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their approach.
conclusion: The method offers a practical route to generate complex non-Gaussian states, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates passive quantum error correction of photon loss at the breakeven point using continuous drives, extending a qubit's lifetime beyond its physical limits.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive schemes could simplify error correction and improve qubit lifetimes.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives in a superconducting circuit, likely involving a bosonic mode coupled to a qubit, to protect against photon loss without active measurements.
result: They achieve error correction at the breakeven point, meaning the corrected qubit lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit, demonstrating the effectiveness of passive protection.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction can be a viable approach to extend qubit coherence, potentially simplifying quantum computing hardware.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and simple intensity detection, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification technique that is invariant to losses.
method: The method employs phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification (OPA) followed by intensity detection. By analyzing the amplified signal, they derive criteria that certify quantum non-Gaussianity without requiring high detection efficiency.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the loss-invariant certification on a heralded quasi-single-photon state, showing that the method can certify non-classicality and non-Gaussianity even under significant losses.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and robust tool for certifying quantum non-Gaussian states, which is valuable for quantum information applications such as quantum computing and communication.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel trapping approach.
method: They design an on-chip magnetic levitation scheme that traps neon particles, which host electron qubits, and analyze its feasibility and tunability.
result: The architecture shows potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, with a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The proposed on-chip levitation architecture could enable scalable electron-on-neon qubits, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard
