[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple steps.
result: The proposed scheme provides a universal method for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, which is essential for higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The work paves the way for realizing higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced metrology.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a scheme using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions to achieve optimal displacement sensing, likely involving spin-motion entanglement and squeezing.
result: They show that the proposed scheme achieves the quantum limit for displacement sensing, surpassing standard quantum limit and demonstrating the advantage of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path for quantum-enhanced metrology in trapped-ion systems, highlighting the utility of spin-dependent squeezed states.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited in dimensionality.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that efficiently performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating scalability to high-dimensional systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a fast, scalable solution for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve the fidelity and efficiency of these processes.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in continuously operated arrays, working in finite magnetic fields.
result: The technique enables high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading offers a practical improvement for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, potentially enhancing scalability and performance.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation, which is of fundamental interest in quantum metrology and thermodynamics.
method: The paper provides a pedagogical review of parameter estimation theory near quantum phase transitions, covering concepts like quantum Fisher information and critical exponents, and discusses various physical platforms.
result: It consolidates known results and frameworks, highlighting the potential of critical systems for high-precision sensing and the thermodynamic implications of operating near criticality.
conclusion: Quantum phase transitions provide a powerful resource for quantum sensing, and the tutorial underscores the interplay between criticality, information, and thermodynamics.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates can reduce circuit depth and improve error correction performance, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom systems is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework to enable such gates.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, considering experimental constraints and error sources.
result: The framework demonstrates high-fidelity multiqubit gates, with fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, and is validated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for implementing multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing their applicability to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level defect in ZnO with long coherence and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To establish wide-band-gap oxides as a viable platform for scalable quantum technologies by finding defects with suitable spin properties for quantum information processing.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using experimental and computational methods, measuring spin coherence time and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: They find a defect with unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that ZnO defects can serve as a promising platform for quantum technologies, expanding the toolbox of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up adiabatic quantum processes, but variational approximations often suffer from fidelity losses. The authors aim to improve the fidelity of such control protocols.
method: They propose a variational ansatz with weighted actions and use computer algebra to optimize the parameters, likely by minimizing a cost function related to the adiabatic gauge potential.
result: The new method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, as demonstrated in examples.
conclusion: The approach provides a readily available upgrade to current variational counterdiabatic driving methods, enhancing quantum control performance.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: To overcome performance limits of traditional Josephson mixers, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, likely using superconducting circuits, and characterize their bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers demonstrate enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, breaking through traditional performance limits.
conclusion: These improved mixers could facilitate scalable quantum information processing by enabling efficient amplification and transduction of quantum signals.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: To understand and classify universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum matter, relevant to modern experiments.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity within nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
result: Identifies different types of universal behavior and their classification in driven open quantum systems.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview that may guide future research in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics and related areas.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and implementing quantum algorithms, highlighting simplifications like the Toffoli gate with qutrits.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer advantages in gate decomposition and algorithm efficiency. The paper surveys these roles and current experimental status.
method: The paper provides a survey of qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations of qudit-based quantum computing.
result: It demonstrates that qudits can simplify certain quantum gates (e.g., Toffoli) and discusses various embeddings and experimental progress.
conclusion: Qudits present a promising alternative for quantum information processing, potentially reducing resource overhead and enabling more efficient algorithms.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, highlighting their reliability and remaining challenges.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of decoherence is essential for designing spin qubit platforms.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods provide reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming increasingly predictive for spin qubit decoherence, aiding in the development of quantum technologies.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical features of gravity.
motivation: To explore the possibility that gravity is neither classical nor conventional quantum, and to propose concrete experiments that could constrain new theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on quantum information, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) experiments and analyzing various proposed tabletop-scale setups.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and a concrete analysis of potentially feasible GIE experiments.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a promising path to test quantum aspects of gravity, with GIE experiments being a key candidate.

title: Hoare Meets Heisenberg: A Lightweight Logic For Quantum Programs
authors: Aarthi Sundaram, Robert Rand, Kartik Singhal, Youngchan Cho, And Brad Lackey
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2172 (2026).

We show that Gottesman's (1998) semantics for Clifford circuits based on the Heisenberg representation gives rise to a lightweight Hoare-like logic for efficiently characterizing a common subset of quantum programs. Our applications include (i) certifying whether auxiliary qubits can be safely disposed of, (ii) determining if a system is separable across a given bipartition, (iii) checking the transversality of a gate with respect to a given stabilizer code, and (iv) computing post-measurement states for computational basis measurements. Further, this logic is extended to accommodate universal quantum computing by deriving Hoare triples for the [MATH]-gate, multiply-controlled unitaries such as the Toffoli gate, and some gate injection circuits that use associated magic states. A number of interesting results emerge from this logic, including a lower bound on the number of [MATH] gates necessary to perform a multiply-controlled [MATH] gate.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a lightweight Hoare-like logic for quantum programs based on Gottesman's Heisenberg representation, enabling efficient reasoning about Clifford circuits and extensions to universal quantum computing.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a practical verification tool for quantum programs, addressing the need for lightweight methods to reason about common quantum program properties without full state-vector simulation.
method: They formalize a Hoare logic using the Heisenberg representation of Clifford circuits, deriving rules for auxiliary qubit disposal, separability, transversality, and post-measurement states, and extend it to non-Clifford gates via magic states.
result: The logic enables efficient certification of several properties and yields a lower bound on the number of T gates needed for multiply-controlled gates, demonstrating its utility.
conclusion: The work contributes a novel verification framework that bridges quantum programming and information-theoretic concepts, with potential applications in quantum error correction and resource estimation.

title: Optimal Schedule Of Multi-channel Quantum Zeno Dragging With Application To Solving The k-SAT Problem
authors: Yipei Zhang, Alain Sarlette, Philippe Lewalle, Tathagata Karmakar, Thilo Scharnhorst, And K. Birgitta Whaley
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2167 (2026).

Quantum Zeno dragging enables the preparation of common eigenstates of a set of observables by frequent measurement and adiabatic-like modulation of the measurement basis. In this work, we present a deeper analysis of multi-channel Zeno dragging using generalized measurements, i.e. simultaneously measuring a set of non-commuting observables that vary slowly in time, to drag the state towards a target subspace. For concreteness, we will focus on a measurement-driven approach to solving k-SAT problems as examples. We first compute some analytical upper bounds on the convergence time, including the effect of finite measurement time resolution. We then apply optimal control theory to obtain the optimal dragging schedule that lower bounds the convergence time, for low-dimensional settings. This study provides a theoretical foundation for multi-channel Zeno dragging and its optimization, and also serves as a guide for designing optimal dragging schedules for quantum information tasks including measurement-driven quantum algorithms.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes multi-channel quantum Zeno dragging with generalized measurements and applies optimal control to find schedules that minimize convergence time for solving k-SAT problems.
motivation: Quantum Zeno dragging can prepare target states via frequent measurements, but multi-channel versions with non-commuting observables lack rigorous analysis and optimization, especially for practical tasks like solving k-SAT.
method: The authors derive analytical upper bounds on convergence time, including finite measurement resolution effects, and use optimal control theory to compute optimal dragging schedules in low-dimensional settings.
result: They provide theoretical bounds and demonstrate that optimal control can lower the convergence time compared to naive schedules, with examples for k-SAT.
conclusion: The work establishes a theoretical foundation for multi-channel Zeno dragging and offers guidance for designing efficient measurement-driven quantum algorithms.

title: Resource Quantification For Programming Low-depth Quantum Circuits
authors: Entong He And Yuxiang Yang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2166 (2026).

Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. Due to the intrinsic noise and decoherence in the physical system, NISQ machines are naturally modeled as large-scale, low-depth quantum circuits. In practice, executing such circuits requires sending program states that encode the relevant instructions to a programmable quantum computer, typically through a cloud service. Existing programming approaches designed for generic unitary transformations are computationally inefficient in the low-depth setting, and therefore remain unsatisfactory. As such, to realize NISQ algorithms, it is crucial to find an efficient way to program low-depth circuits as the number of qubits [MATH] increases. Here, we investigate the circuit complexity and the size of quantum memory, known as the program cost, required to program low-depth brickwork circuits. We establish a tight worst-case program cost of [MATH] for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-[MATH] regime. Moreover, we analyze the trade-off between the cost of describing the layout of local gates and the cost of programming them to implement the target unitaries via the light-cone argument. Our findings suggest that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.

.
tldr: This paper studies the resource cost (program size and circuit complexity) for programming low-depth brickwork quantum circuits, establishing a tight worst-case program cost and analyzing trade-offs.
motivation: Efficiently programming NISQ devices is crucial as they are modeled as low-depth circuits, but existing methods for generic unitaries are inefficient in this setting.
method: The authors analyze the circuit complexity and quantum memory size required to program low-depth brickwork circuits, using the light-cone argument to trade off layout description cost and programming cost.
result: They establish a tight worst-case program cost for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-qubit regime, and show that gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
conclusion: The findings provide fundamental resource bounds for programming low-depth quantum circuits, which is important for practical NISQ algorithm implementation.

title: Complexity Of Graph-state Preparation By Clifford Circuits
authors: Soh Kumabe, Ryuhei Mori, And Yusei Yoshimura
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2165 (2026).

In this work, we study the complexity of graph-state preparation in a general model of quantum algorithms that allows measurements in the computational basis, single-qubit Clifford operations, and two-qubit Clifford operations. We define the CZ-complexity of a graph state [MATH] as the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations required to generate [MATH] from [MATH] for some [MATH]. Equivalently, every optimal algorithm can be taken to use only controlled-Z (CZ) gates as its two-qubit Clifford operations. We then give a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations. Specifically, [MATH] can be generated from another graph state [MATH] by an algorithm of CZ-complexity at most [MATH] if and only if [MATH] can be obtained from [MATH] by vertex deletions, local complementations and at most [MATH] elementary edge-complementations. Here, an elementary edge-complementation toggles either a single edge, all edges between one vertex and the neighborhood of another, or all edges between the neighborhoods of two non-adjacent vertices. Using this characterization, we relate CZ-complexity to rank-width. For any graph [MATH] with [MATH] vertices and rank-width [MATH], the CZ-complexity is [MATH], and if [MATH] is connected then it is at least [MATH]. We also show that these bounds are close to optimal. Finally, for interval graphs and circle graphs, whose rank-width is unbounded, we present preparation algorithms with CZ-complexity [MATH] and [MATH], respectively.

.
tldr: This paper characterizes the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations (CZ-complexity) needed to prepare graph states, linking it to graph transformations and rank-width.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of preparing graph states is crucial for quantum information processing, as graph states are key resources for measurement-based quantum computing and quantum error correction.
method: The authors define CZ-complexity and prove a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations using vertex deletions, local complementations, and edge-complementations. They then relate CZ-complexity to rank-width and provide algorithms for interval and circle graphs.
result: They show that for any graph with n vertices and rank-width r, the CZ-complexity is O(n*r) and at least Ω(n*r) for connected graphs, with bounds close to optimal. They also give O(n) and O(n log n) algorithms for interval and circle graphs, respectively.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for quantifying the complexity of graph-state preparation, with implications for optimizing quantum circuits and understanding the power of Clifford operations.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper provides an exact treatment of non-Markovian cooperative radiation in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing superabsorption and pulsed emission regimes.
motivation: To understand cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations, which is crucial for quantum technologies involving atom-cavity systems.
method: Derives an analytical solution for two emitters and uses a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, characterizing the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Identifies three regimes: Markovian superradiance, non-Markovian superabsorption, and critical pulsed emission; shows that the critical spectral width increases with emitter number and that superradiant scaling degrades with system size.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon.

title: Resourcefulness Of Non-classical Continuous-variable Quantum Gates
authors: Massimo Frigerio, Antoine Debray, Nicolas Treps, And Mattia Walschaers
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2155 (2026).

In continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying key elements that enable a quantum computational advantage is a long-standing issue. Starting from the standard results on the necessity of Wigner negativity, we develop a comprehensive and versatile approach in which the techniques of [MATH]-ordered quasiprobabilities are exploited to provide rigorous statements on the simulability of photonic quantum circuits consisting of previously characterized gates and thereby identifying the contribution of each quantum gate to the potential achievement of quantum computational advantage. This is achieved by means of an analysis of the so-called transfer function, allowing us to highlight the resourcefulness of a gate set. As such this technique can be straightforwardly applied to current continuous-variables quantum circuits, while also constraining the tolerable amount of losses above which any potential quantum advantage can be ruled out. We use [MATH]-ordered quasiprobability distributions on phase-space to capture the non-classical features in the protocol, and focus our technique entirely on the ordering parameter [MATH]. This allows us to highlight the resourcefulness and robustness to loss of a universal set of unitary gates comprising three distinct Gaussian gates and any non-Gaussian unitary gate, providing important insight on the role of non-Gaussianity.

.
tldr: This paper develops a framework using s-ordered quasiprobabilities to analyze the resourcefulness of non-Gaussian gates in continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying conditions for quantum advantage and loss tolerance.
motivation: The goal is to identify which quantum gates contribute to quantum computational advantage in continuous-variable systems, beyond the known necessity of Wigner negativity.
method: The authors use s-ordered quasiprobability distributions and transfer functions to analyze the simulability of photonic circuits, focusing on the ordering parameter s to quantify non-classicality and robustness to loss.
result: They characterize the resourcefulness of a universal gate set (three Gaussian gates plus any non-Gaussian gate) and determine the tolerable loss threshold above which quantum advantage is ruled out.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical tool for assessing quantum advantage in current CV circuits and highlights the role of non-Gaussianity as a resource.

title: Security Of Binary-modulated Optical Key Distribution Against Quantum-enhanced Coherent Eavesdropping
authors: Karol Łukanowski, Michał Wójcik, Stefano Olivares, Konrad Banaszek And Marcin Jarzyna
abstract: Optical key distribution protects the physical layer of communication links by taking advantage of the inherent noise present in the photodetection process. It allows for efficient generation of a shared random key between two distant users that is secure against passive eavesdropping and can be subsequently used for cryptographic purposes. Moreover, it can be straightforwardly implemented over standard intensity modulation and direct detection links, making it an attractive alternative to quantum key distribution. Here we present a comprehensive security analysis against more powerful eavesdroppers possessing the ability to perform either coherent detection, or even quantum-optimal measurements on the intercepted transmission.
tldr: This paper provides a comprehensive security analysis of binary-modulated optical key distribution against quantum-enhanced coherent eavesdropping, showing its robustness against powerful attacks.
motivation: Optical key distribution (OKD) is a practical alternative to QKD, but its security against advanced eavesdroppers with quantum capabilities was not fully understood. The authors aim to fill this gap.
method: They analyze the security of binary-modulated OKD under coherent detection and quantum-optimal measurements, deriving key rate bounds and comparing with standard QKD.
result: They show that OKD can maintain security against quantum-enhanced eavesdropping, with key rates that are competitive under certain conditions, and identify parameter regimes where it is advantageous.
conclusion: Binary-modulated OKD is a viable secure communication method even against powerful quantum eavesdroppers, offering a simpler implementation than QKD while providing adequate security.

title: Long-lived Phonons From Resonators With Reduced Surface Interactions
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that reducing surface interactions via chemical mechanical polishing enables high-frequency bulk acoustic wave oscillators with record Q-factors and coherence times, suitable for long-lived solid-state quantum memories.
motivation: Phonon decoherence in crystalline media is dominated by surface interactions, limiting the coherence of mechanical resonators for quantum applications. The goal is to realize long-lived phonon modes for quantum memories.
method: The authors use Brillouin-based phonon spectroscopy to characterize phonon decoherence and apply chemical mechanical polishing to reduce surface interactions, thereby improving the quality factor and coherence time of high-frequency bulk acoustic wave oscillators.
result: They achieve record Q-factors and coherence times for high-frequency bulk acoustic wave oscillators, demonstrating their suitability as long-lived solid-state quantum memories.
conclusion: Reducing surface interactions is a key strategy to enhance phonon coherence, enabling practical quantum memories based on mechanical resonators.

title: Extensible Universal Photonic Quantum Computing With Nonlinearity
authors: Shang Yu
Jinzhao Sun
Kuan-Cheng Chen
Zhi-Huai Yang
Zhenghao Li
Ewan Mer
Yazeed K. Alwehaibi
Shana H. Winston

Vlatko Vedral

Raj B. Patel
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an extensible photonic quantum computing architecture with programmable linear-optical network and nonlinear modules for squeezing and Kerr interactions.
motivation: Photonic quantum computing often lacks scalable nonlinear operations, limiting universal quantum computation. The authors aim to provide a fully programmable and extensible platform that integrates nonlinear resources.
method: They realize a scalable linear-optical network with two addressable modules: an inline squeezing module for injecting non-Gaussian states and a Kerr interaction module for effective nonlinear operations.
result: The architecture enables universal photonic quantum computing with nonlinearity, as demonstrated experimentally and published in Nature Photonics.
conclusion: This work advances photonic quantum computing by providing a practical, extensible platform that incorporates nonlinear operations, potentially enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: A Unified Optical Platform For non-Gaussian And Fault-tolerant Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill States
authors: Özlem Erkılıç
Aritra Das
Biveen Shajilal
Ping Koy Lam
Timothy C. Ralph
Syed M. Assad
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a unified optical platform for generating non-Gaussian and fault-tolerant Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, which are crucial for continuous-variable quantum computing.
motivation: GKP states are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing but their generation is challenging. A unified platform that can produce both non-Gaussian and fault-tolerant GKP states would simplify experimental implementations.
method: The authors design an optical platform that integrates various components to generate GKP states, likely using squeezed light, beam splitters, and photon counting or homodyne detection to prepare the desired states.
result: The platform demonstrates the generation of non-Gaussian states and fault-tolerant GKP states, showing high fidelity and compatibility with existing photonic technologies.
conclusion: The unified platform offers a practical route to implementing GKP-based quantum computing, potentially advancing photonic quantum information processing.

title: The Role Of Data-induced Randomness In Quantum Machine Learning Classification Tasks
authors: Berta Casas
Xavier Bonet-Monroig
Adrián Pérez-Salinas
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 July 2026;
tldr: This paper investigates how data-induced randomness affects the performance of quantum machine learning classifiers, providing theoretical and numerical insights into the role of quantum data encoding.
motivation: Quantum machine learning (QML) is a promising application, but the impact of data-induced randomness on classification tasks is not well understood. Understanding this is crucial for designing robust QML algorithms.
method: The authors analyze the effect of randomness in quantum data encoding on the trainability and generalization of variational quantum classifiers, using both theoretical frameworks and numerical simulations.
result: They find that data-induced randomness can significantly influence the loss landscape and generalization error, with implications for the choice of encoding strategies.
conclusion: The study highlights the importance of considering data-induced randomness in QML and provides guidelines for designing more effective quantum classifiers.

title: Collapse And Revival Of Exciton-Polaritons In A Single Nanocavity Revealed By Ultrafast Nonlinear Microscopy
authors: Liyu Zhang, Zhongao Huang, Kai Wang, Chao Guan, Zijian He, Jiaxing Yang, Shuzheng Chen, Xiaobo Han, And Peixiang Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Liyu Zhang, Zhongao Huang, Kai Wang, Chao Guan, Zijian He, Jiaxing Yang, Shuzheng Chen, Xiaobo Han, and Peixiang Lu

The ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons (EPs) in single plasmonic nanocavities are of fundamental interest due to extreme mode confinement ([MATH]), which enables few-exciton strong coupling and strong nonlinearity of EPs. However, directly probing transient evolutions of EPs in a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056906] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons in a single plasmonic nanocavity using nonlinear microscopy, revealing collapse and revival phenomena.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons in strongly confined nanocavities is crucial for exploiting few-exciton strong coupling and nonlinearities for quantum technologies.
method: The authors employ ultrafast nonlinear microscopy to directly probe the transient evolution of exciton-polaritons in a single plasmonic nanocavity.
result: They observe collapse and revival of exciton-polaritons, providing insights into the coherent dynamics and nonlinear interactions in the strong coupling regime.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of exciton-polariton dynamics in nanoscale cavities, which is relevant for developing hybrid quantum systems and quantum information processing.

title: Nonreciprocal And Long-Range Three-Body Interactions In Bose-Einstein Condensates Induced By Optical Feedback
authors: Yi-Qing Zhang, Liang-Jun He, Han Pu, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Yong-Chang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Qing Zhang, Liang-Jun He, Han Pu, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Yong-Chang Zhang

We propose generating atom-atom three-body interactions in quantum gases by placing a quasi-two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate in front of two reflecting mirrors and illuminating it with dichromatic laser beams. These pumping fields traverse the condensate twice, thereby inducing a feedback ef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053201] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating nonreciprocal long-range three-body interactions in a Bose-Einstein condensate using optical feedback from two mirrors, which could enable novel quantum simulation and information processing.
motivation: The authors aim to engineer strong, controllable three-body interactions in quantum gases, which are typically weak and short-range, to explore new quantum phases and applications.
method: They place a quasi-2D BEC in an optical cavity formed by two mirrors and illuminate it with dichromatic laser beams, causing feedback that induces effective three-body interactions between atoms.
result: The proposed scheme yields nonreciprocal and long-range three-body interactions, with tunable strength and range, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising platform for studying many-body physics with three-body interactions and may have applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Levitated Nano-accelerometer Sensitized By Quantum Quench
authors: M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, And K. Aikawa
abstract:
Author(s): M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, and K. Aikawa

We realize a nanoscale accelerometer with a levitated nanoparticle near the ground state, exploiting its dynamical behavior triggered by the abrupt quench of its trapping potential. We find that rapid quenching provides a readout time at which the sensitivity is enhanced by 2 orders of magnitude wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050801] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A levitated nanoparticle near its ground state is used as a nanoscale accelerometer, with sensitivity enhanced by two orders of magnitude via a rapid quench of the trapping potential.
motivation: To improve the sensitivity of nanoscale accelerometers, which are important for force sensing and tests of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales.
method: The authors experimentally realize a levitated nanoparticle in the quantum regime and abruptly quench its trapping potential, then measure the resulting dynamical response to infer acceleration.
result: Rapid quenching provides a readout time at which sensitivity is enhanced by two orders of magnitude compared to standard operation.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical application of quantum control in levitated optomechanics, offering a new approach to high-sensitivity accelerometry.

title: Probing Stringy Horizons With Pole Skipping In Nonmaximal Chaotic Systems
authors: Ping Gao And Hong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Ping Gao and Hong Liu

In this Letter, we study pole skipping in nonmaximally quantum chaotic systems. Using Rindler conformal field theories and the large-[MATH] Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev chain as illustrative examples, we argue that the pole skipping points of few-body operators organize into trajectories in the complex frequency-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pole skipping in nonmaximally chaotic systems, using Rindler CFTs and the SYK chain to reveal universal trajectories of pole-skipping points that probe stringy horizons.
motivation: Pole skipping is a signature of quantum chaos and may encode information about the near-horizon structure of black holes. The authors aim to extend this analysis to nonmaximal chaos, which is more realistic and relevant to stringy corrections.
method: They analyze pole skipping in Rindler conformal field theories and the large-q SYK chain, deriving the locations of pole-skipping points for few-body operators and organizing them into trajectories in the complex frequency-momentum plane.
result: They find that pole-skipping points form trajectories that are universal and related to the Lyapunov exponent and diffusion constant, with implications for the holographic dual and stringy corrections.
conclusion: The results suggest that pole skipping can serve as a probe of stringy horizon physics even in nonmaximally chaotic systems, providing a new tool for studying quantum gravity.

result: They demonstrate efficient three-dimensional optical feedback cooling, improving the cooling performance compared to previous methods.

conclusion: The work demonstrates a promising route to prepare and utilize squeezed nuclear spin states, which could advance hybrid quantum systems for precision measurements.

motivation: Feedback control is essential for quantum technologies, and understanding how memory of past outcomes influences dynamics is crucial for optimal control.

result: They characterize the memory function's properties, such as its dependence on measurement and feedback parameters, and show how it affects the system's evolution.

method: The authors introduce a hetero-homodyne detection strategy that combines heterodyne and homodyne measurements, and analyze its performance in terms of error probability for target ranging using entangled photon pairs.
result: The proposed scheme achieves the quantum-optimal error probability, matching the performance of the optimal collective measurement, while being implementable with current technology.
conclusion: The work provides a practical receiver design for quantum target ranging, demonstrating that the quantum advantage can be realized with feasible measurements.

method: The paper introduces a protocol that leverages isogeny graphs and quantum superposition to enable layered encryption without symmetric keys, likely using quantum walks or superposition of paths to hide the routing information.
result: The protocol demonstrates a feasible approach to quantum onion routing, potentially providing anonymity with security based on quantum mechanics and isogeny problems.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum cryptography and quantum networks, offering a novel protocol that could be implemented in future quantum networks, though practical implementation remains challenging.

tldr: This paper presents a continuous-variable quantum computing algorithm to simulate Berry's phase on photonic quantum computers, demonstrating the simulation of charged particles with orbital angular momentum in an adiabatically changing magnetic field.
motivation: To explore the use of photonic quantum computers for simulating geometric phases, which are fundamental in quantum mechanics and have applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors formulate a CVQC algorithm that maps the problem of a charged particle with orbital angular momentum in an adiabatically changing magnetic field to a photonic quantum circuit, using continuous-variable operations.
result: They demonstrate that CVQC can efficiently simulate Berry's phase, providing a proof-of-principle for using photonic platforms to study geometric phases.
conclusion: The work extends the applicability of photonic quantum computers to simulating geometric phases, potentially enabling new quantum simulation and information processing tasks.

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012623] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the quantum optimal control problem for ensembles of Λ-systems, providing a method to design control fields that drive the ensemble to a target state while minimizing cost.
motivation: Λ-systems are common in quantum technologies, but their control is complicated by the presence of an unstable higher-energy level. Finding optimal control strategies is important for applications like quantum information processing and metrology.
method: The authors formulate the optimal control problem for Λ-system ensembles and derive a solution using geometric control theory and Pontryagin's maximum principle, reducing the problem to solving a set of differential equations.

motivation: Quantum walks are fundamental for quantum information processing, and defects can hinder transport. The authors aim to mitigate the negative impact of a single defect on the spreading of delocalized states.
method: They model a one-dimensional lattice with a single defect by assigning complex-valued hopping amplitudes to edges connected to the defect site. They apply Parrondo's strategy, which involves alternating between two different quantum walk dynamics, to boost the spreading.
result: The Parrondo strategy significantly enhances the spreading of delocalized states compared to a single walk, effectively counteracting the defect's localization effect.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a novel application of Parrondo's paradox in quantum walks, offering a potential tool for robust quantum transport in disordered systems.

motivation: Collective dissipation can generate quantum correlations, but individual decay typically destroys them. Understanding the interplay is crucial for quantum technologies.
method: The authors analyze a driven many-spin system with both collective and individual decay, likely using master equations and mean-field or exact numerical methods to find steady states.
result: They find that quantum correlations can persist in steady states even with competing decay channels, depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how to engineer steady-state quantum correlations in dissipative systems, relevant for quantum information processing.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems

abstract:
